messages: maria: Quick summary of the rw-large-v2 quant bakeoff results — dropping INT8 AWQ profile saved ~3.2x p50 CPU/GPU latency and cut token cost by ~45%, but we saw task-specific regressions on Legal-QA and pretty consistent markdown/table formatting errors on code-gen workloads. alex: Can you paste the specific deltas? numbers + tests? maria: Sure — overall EM on general QA down 0.8pp, Legal-QA EM down 7.1pp, hallucination rate (+confab) for long-context QA up ~4.5pp. Code-gen formatting failures (misplaced / lost backticks) ~3.8% vs 0.4% baseline. jin: Those formatting errors smell like tokenization/bytepair issues post-quant. Are we seeing token id shifts for markup tokens? maria: We did a quick diff of token id histograms — some higher-frequency markup tokens shifted probability mass. Not huge but enough to break structured outputs in tight templates. lena: Do we have the eval-bot run links for the full per-task logs? eval-bot: Perf scoreboard: https://internal.redwood/evals/runs/1976543209 — includes example traces, per-task deltas, and seed-level stats. :white_check_mark: carter: Re: deployment profile — we were planning to push AWQ-int8 as default for Dedicated low-latency tier. Given these deltas, maybe a selective routing policy is better: keep FP8/FP16 for Legal-QA and structured outputs, AWQ-int8 for free-text chat. alex: Agreed. We can do policy by route. Quick config sketch: ``` routes: - match: {route: "/legal/*"} model_variant: rw-large-v2-fp8 max_batch_ms: 10 - match: {route: "/chat/*"} model_variant: rw-large-v2-awq-int8 max_batch_ms: 30 ``` jin: Also try prefix-KV caching for legal docs; most hallucinations were when context > 4k tokens and AWQ somehow degraded KV fidelity. lena: Can we reproduce locally with smaller run? what's the minimal repro? maria: Repro steps in the eval run: use legal-qa dataset shard 3, seed 42, prompt template A2, compare variants with temperature=0.0, max_new_tokens=512. Command: ```bash ./eval_runner --model rw-large-v2 --variant awq-int8 --dataset legal-qa/shard3 --seed 42 --output traces/1976543210-awq ``` carter: I ran that with pmap pinned and saw the same EM drop. Attaching short trace snippet: ``` TRACE: prompt_len=2048, kv_hits=0.72, avg_logprob_drop=0.18 OUTPUT: "The contract states..." -> hallucinated clause "subject to regulatory oversight X" ``` alex: Could be quant noise compounding over long prefix leading to cascaded errors in attention. We should try hybrid quant: AWQ-int8 for MLPs, FP8 for attention/kv. Any throughput hit estimate? eval-bot: Hybrid profile simulation estimating throughput: AWQ-int8-all: 1.0x baseline p50, hybrid(attn fp8): 1.6x p50, fp8-all: 2.2x p50. Latency/cost numbers in run page. maria: For next steps I suggest: 1) narrow repro on legal-qa and table templates (small shard) 2) try hybrid attention-FP8 + AWQ for rest 3) add unit eval that checks for markdown/table tokens preserved 4) update rollout to route sensitive endpoints to fp8. lena: I'll add the markdown-preservation unit to the eval harness — simple regex check for matching code-block fences and balanced tags. carter: I'll prototype hybrid compile flags and run a 10k sample bakeoff. Planning window: 24h. jin: If hybrid doesn't fix hallucinations, next is seed-ensemble voting for legal-qa (cheap) or fall back to fp8 for that route. alex: Sounds good. Also make sure alerting on production SLIs for StructuredOutputErrors spikes after rollout. eng-oncall should get a pager if StructuredOutputErrors > 0.5% over 10m. maria: Noted. I'll update the canary plan. deploy-bot just posted the canary run for the AWQ rollout earlier — small traffic tilt 2% to AWQ-int8 at 15:00 UTC. deploy-bot: Canary summary: 2% traffic to rw-large-v2-awq-int8 — p50 42ms -> 13ms; StructuredOutputErrors 0.9% (was 0.3% baseline); Legal-QA EM delta -6.9pp. Rolling back after alerts triggered. lena: Thanks — rollback confirmed. maria: I'll open an RFC for hybrid variant + route policy and tag eng-runtime/eng-ml. Will include perf sims and eval links. alex: Please also include a minimal sample prompt set so SEs can test integrations (markdown tables + small contract clauses). maria: Will do. Thx all. :pray:
